title: Launch and diagnostic: building routines that survive a schedule change
focus: building routines that survive a schedule change
essentialQuestion: What has to keep happening when no one reminds me?
keyPoints: A durable routine uses a clear cue, minimum viable action, flexible time window, and restart rule so a schedule change does not turn one disruption into abandonment.
A durable plan names the goal, constraints, feasible options, support and backup routes, plus the evidence or condition that should trigger review and revision.

For building routines that survive a schedule change, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build an independent maintenance system with a normal-week version, a hard-week fallback version, and a written restart procedure. Progress is described in terms of behaviors kept, never body measurements.
studentTask: Build a decision organizer for a fictional person working on building routines that survive a schedule change. Record the goal, two influences or constraints, two options, the safest feasible choice, a support or backup route, and the evidence that would trigger a later revision.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in building routines that survive a schedule change; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
